newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open sharply lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open sharply lower Monday, with blame still pinned on a gold market rattled by the Bundesbank's bullion reserves reevaluation plan, and weakness in silver and platinum, dealers said.
COMEX June gold was called off $1.50 to $2.00 from Friday's close of $344.90 an ounce after trading from $345.30 to $342.90 on ACCESS.
Early gold bullion was quoted at $341.65/95.
COMEX July silver was called flat to 1.00 cent lower after trading from $4.72 to $4.655 on ACCESS.
Many Continental European markets were shut Monday.
The financial markets were also awaiting the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee to see if interest rates would be hiked or left unchanged.
London gold fixed lower this morning at $343.35, down from $344.50 Friday afternoon.
COMEX gold stocks Friday were unchanged at 895,028 ounces, while the exchange's silver stocks rose 283,589 ounces to 192,158,881 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum was called off $1.50 to $2.00 from Friday's close of $391.20, with NYMEX June palladium called down $1.00 to $2.00 from Friday's finish of $172.10.
